target_customer: Residential property managers and landlords with scattered rentals who pay per listing or subscription
problem: Vacant units cost money while managers manually list, pre-qualify and schedule showings.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced per rental listing credit, later subscription

founders.name: James Barrett
founders.background_notes: Became a landlord in 2009 per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web app with listing syndication, phone and email pre-qualification and scheduling; integration with locks added complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow integrations with property management systems helped, but the core was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Property management platforms partnered rather than copied; Buildium later powered its Showings Coordinator with Tenant Turner and AppFolio integrated it.

market_need_then: Founders were landlords who felt the vacancy pain; the company grew from a tenant screening idea in 2013 into leasing software.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive pun on turning units over; little brand coverage found.

pivots.to: Leasing automation software for property managers
pivots.why: Local press says it shifted toward selling leasing software; exact date not given.

outcome_analysis: Tenant Turner started as a tenant screening idea by VCU friends, took 390 thousand dollars from Richmond angels in 2015 and became a leasing automation tool integrated with major property platforms. It was reportedly acquired around 2025 at an undisclosed price, suggesting a modest, capital efficient outcome.
notes: Acquisition rests on one competitor blog (RentEngine) in January 2025 naming GSV; Seedtable says acquired by PropertyTek (Greater Sum Ventures) January 2024. Date and buyer unverified. Other rounds (CIT GAP Fund, a March 2016 round, YC) are in aggregators without amounts so not recorded. Company site was not fetched. ShowMojo and Rently appear only in later comparisons, so the dated competitor list is empty.
